newsitem.title: POLAND: Daiwa sees Warsaw bourse at 18,500 year-end.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa sees Warsaw bourse at 18,500 year-end.

text.p: The Polish bourse, now trading at 10.3 times 1997 earnings and 8.5 times 1998 earnings, should end the year at 18,500 points, Daiwa Europe Limited said in its June Central/Eastern Europe Equity Strategy Report.

"The WIG (main index) may stay range-bound in the very near term. We remain moderately overweight (on Poland), though, due to the positive medium-term outlook. Our year-end WIG target is 18,500," the report dated May 30 said.

Daiwa said the Polish bourse was currently fairly priced with its 1997 and 1998 price-earnings ratios putting it in the middle of the Eastern European spectrum and below emerging markets in other regions.

It saw the Warsaw bourse flat until at least September's parliamentary vote, which added uncertainty, but said its favourable medium-term view was based on Poland's relatively high market transparency, liquidity and economic fundamentals.
"We do not anticipate a Czech-style currency attack, since Polish fundamentals are in better shape," the report said.

Daiwa said money would stay off the secondary market in coming weeks also due to Poland's heavy IPO schedule, public offerings in other countries such as Hungary and increased competition from fixed-income instruments.
But the Polish IPOs would provide more large-cap selection and liquidity in the medium term.
Daiwa liked Mostosta Zabrze and Gorazdze in the construction sector and said Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw prices should continue to be boosted from their planned merger.
Robust consumer demand would help Jutrzenka and Wedel while in the drugs sector Daiwa said Jelfa was a good long-term play.
Daiwa said disappointing earnings made it neutral on Polish banks.
